The '''Theed Hangar''', also known as the '''Royal Starport''', was a large facility located alongside the triple-domed [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]] [[Plasma Refinery Complex|refinery]] in the city of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]], the capital of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. The headquarters of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] and [[Naboo Royal Space Fighter Corps/Legends|Starfighter Corps]], the hangar housed the planet's [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighter]] fleet and the monarch's Royal [[Starship/Legends|starships]] and air-traffic control facility.

Equipped with sensitive radar array-based air-traffic control, tactical computer stations and a secret subterranean tunnel link to the palace, the hangar played a pivotal role in the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation's]] [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invasion of the planet]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] and became a rallying point for the eventual uprising against the occupation.

==History==
[[File:Theed_hangar_battle.png|thumb|left|250px|The battle to retake the Hangar in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].]]
During the reign of the [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|King]] [[Bon Tapalo/Legends|Bon Tapalo]], the Naboo were approached by [[Damask Holdings/Legends|Damask Holdings]], an entity within the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]], with an offer of mining and exporting the [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]] that was found in abundance in the planet's core. Despite trepidation at the idea of using primarily offworld businesses to jump-start the plasma industry, Tapalo agreed to the terms of [[Magister]] [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Hego Damask]] as the [[Muun/Legends|Muun]] was planning to back the king's bid for reelection.<ref name="SWDP" />

When construction commenced existing parklands just east of the [[Theed Royal Palace/Legends|Royal Palace]] were removed and the and adjacent the [[Solleu River/Legends|Solleu River]] was rerouted to make room for the triple-domes of the new [[Plasma Refinery Complex]] and the hangar facility. Constructed by [[Outer Rim Construction and Assembly/Legends|Outer Rim Construction and Assembly]], the main hangar was the headquarters of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]]' [[Naboo Royal Space Fighter Corps/Legends|fighter corps]]. By King [[Ars Veruna/Legends|Ars Veruna's]] reign, Naboo had become a major player in the interstellar plasma energy market. However, the planet's plasma exports became a source of dispute with the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] and a strenuous relationship with Magister Damask began to take its toll. Wary of looming conflict with the Federation, King Veruna expanded the role of the fighter corps and upped the budget to purchase new [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighters]].<ref name="SWDP" />

Despite Veruna's attempt to ease his people's fears of invasion, the military expansion only increased the growing discontent with his administration. Seeing Veruna as corrupted and out of touch with the peaceful traditions of the planet, the citizens of Naboo and [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] rallied behind a young girl named [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Naberrie]]. Before demilitarization could occur, the Trade Federation [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invaded]], [[Blockade/Legends|blockading]] the [[Naboo system/Legends|system]] and taking the planet's populace hostage.<ref name="SWDP" />

During the initial stages of the invasion, Queen Amidala and her retinue of [[Handmaiden/Legends|handmaidens]], guards, and [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] protectors were able to briefly [[Capture of Theed/Legends|liberate]] the hangar, fleeing into space aboard the Queen's [[J-type 327 Nubian royal starship/Legends|royal starship]]. Accompanied by the Jedi [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], the Queen traveled to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to inform to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] and request its intervention in the occupation.<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> During the fighting that erupted in the city, [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Kael (officer)|Kael]] of the Queen's Security Forces was pinned down near the building's front annex by [[P-series droideka/Legends|destroyer droids]], but was rescued by [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Gavyn Sykes/Legends|Gavyn Sykes]].<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo]]''</ref>

[[File:Battle_Hangar.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Kenobi, Amidala, Jinn, and a young [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] enter the hangar during the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|storming of the Palace]].]]

Upon the Queen's return to the planet she and the Jedi led an [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|infiltration mission]] to retake the planet. Amidala's forces used hidden tunnels to covertly enter Theed, emerging alongside the hangar building. They were able to swiftly take full control of the facility, freeing hangar personnel including air traffic controllers<ref name="SWCL" /> and [[Bravo Squadron/Legends|Bravo Flight's]] pilots who took to their starfighters and [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|attacked]] the orbital [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|Droid Control Ship]]. Among them was a nine-year old [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] who would inadvertently fly an N-1 starfighter from the hangar to the control ship and destroy it, deactivating the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|droid army]] and bringing about an unlikely victory for the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] in the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Grassy Plains]]. During the battle for the hangar, Jinn and Kenobi assisted the Resistance forces by cutting through the door's power cells to cut off the Trade Federation reinforcements.<ref name="SW:OW">[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']]</ref> When the attacking party went to enter through the main gate for the [[Great Hall (Naboo)/Legends|Hangar's Great Hall]], they were stopped by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], forcing the Jedi into a showdown. Amidala then used another secret tunnel via the Hall to gain access to the Royal Palace. During the [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]], Darth Maul used a destroyed [[Droideka/Legends|droideka]] to open the [[Blast door/Legends|blast door]] leading to the [[Plasma Refinery Complex]], where Jinn met his death and Maul was left for dead after being defeated by Kenobi.<ref name="TPM" /><ref name="Wrath of Darth Maul">''[[The Wrath of Darth Maul]]''</ref> Later, after the battle was over, Kenobi and his new apprentice, Anakin Skywalker, were treated to a parade in the hangar as they left the planet.<ref name="SW:OW" /> [[Nym/Legends|Nym]], [[Vana Sage]], and [[Reti]], allies of the Security Forces, also launched from the hangar as they returned to their occupations.<ref name="SW:SF">[[Star Wars: Starfighter (video game)|''Star Wars: Starfighter'']]</ref>

When Skywalker and Kenobi returned in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] to discover the mystery of [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Nuvo Vindi/Legends|Nuvo Vindi]], they landed in the hangar with their contingent of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]].<ref name="Shadow">{{TCW|Blue Shadow Virus (episode)}}</ref> Shortly after the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in the wake of the Clone Wars and the destruction of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], the Empire began storing weapons inside the hangar, particularly explosives. During a mission that brought a rebel group called the [[Erased]] to Naboo, rebels [[Clive Flax]] and [[Ferus Olin]] destroyed the hangar by setting off the explosives cache hidden within. The Empire temporarily withdrew from Naboo rather than retaliate and thus admit to their illegal weapons storage. Queen [[Apailana/Legends|Apailana]], while regretful of the destruction of the facility and the long process of reconstruction, agreed to the decision.<ref name="DON" />

==Layout==
===Exterior===
A part of the Plasma Refinery Complex in the city of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]], the city's main hangar facility was located in Theed's central district on the bank of the [[Solleu River/Legends|Solleu River]] and the [[Virdugo Plunge/Legends|Virdugo Plunge]]. In Theed, even a military facility demonstrated the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo's]] deep sense of artistic and spiritual expression. A model of Neo-Classical design, the structure had a simple but elegant form; it was both functional and graceful and was far more ornate than the stark utilitarian military facilities on other worlds. Constructed from large sandstone-like stone covered by a ribbed roof, the stone was embedded with a high-tensile [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] support webbing while the roof was lined with blast-proof plates to protect the structure from attack.<ref name="SWCL" />

===Interior===
The entrance to Theed Hangar was located in a small courtyard along the [[Solleu River/Legends|Solleu River]]. Accessed through a large curving arch, the building's interior was dominated by the massive hangar bay. Twice as long as it was wide, the hangar space had a curved ceiling which soared over a polished black floor; electrostatic grates in the floor helped dissipate the pollution levels in the room. Along the length of the room's walls were eight niches, sixteen in all, in which each held three N-1 fighters. A unique feature of the N-1's allowed for their tapered tails to plug into the walls where computer ports received coded battle strategies from the palace battle computer for download into starfighter computer banks. Energy ports in the docking bays delivered high-voltage charge to N-1 fighters from the adjacent generator. On the inner wall of the hangar, a tall archway was sealed with a heavy blast-proof door, beyond which stood the city's generator and Plasma Refinery Complex.<ref name="SWCL" /> Six power cells powered the three doors which led into hangar. The generators could be de-powered from a control panel.<ref name="SW:OW" />

The polished floor of the main flight deck reached a terminus of grey stone at the hangar mouth, which overlooked the plunging cliff face. Stretching from the mouth of the hangar to the far inner wall was a set of [[Electromagnet/Legends|electromagnet]] rails which generated a [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] field designed to slow down all ships entering the facility. While the pilots of the Royal Naboo Security Forces employed both on-board flight computers and air-traffic control to navigate their fighters into the hangar, some experienced pilots created tall-tales, claiming they could eyeball the entrance by monitoring the affect of the wind on the nearby waterfall. Four flight guidance beacons adorned the hangar mouth, as well as two statues of the Naboo [[Goddess of security and safekeeping/Legends|Goddess of Security and Safekeeping]]. The facility's main deck was retractable, allowing ships to be lowered or raised from the underground maintenance deck directly below.<ref name="SWCL" />

[[File:Theed_Hangar_BSV.png|thumb|right|250px|[[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry/Legends|LAAT/is]] docked on the main flight deck.]]

A single story level resembling the main deck's architectural design, the maintenance deck was home to the [[Theed Palace Space Vessel Engineering Corps/Legends|Theed Palace Space Vessel Engineering Corps]] who were responsible for the construction of Naboo space craft and their constant servicing and refitting. Overhead cranes ran on rails overhead and diagnostic stations allow maintenance teams to check the operating systems on any star craft in the fleet. Mobile maintenance and refueling vehicles maneuvered about the floor, providing flexible support to spacecraft in any of the repair bays along the side of the maintenance deck. Along the outer wall, a holding area for the fleets many [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]] was where utility droids were prepared for onboard flight support assignments.<ref name="SWCL" />

The highest chamber in the hangar was located above the flight deck in the facility's large cupola. Smaller then the neighboring refinery, the domed structure housed the city's air traffic control nerve center, staffed by specialized members of the security force. The center of the chamber was occupied by a large array of dishes and computer equipment surrounded by a ring of power transmitters capable of degrading and burning out the radar systems of enemy craft. Along the outer wall were work stations where controllers operated the guidance system which used [[Tractor beam/Legends|traction mechanics]]. Embedded into the large lintel-like feature above the flight entrance, the equipment guided spacecraft into the hangar automatically by locking onto their flight coordinates.<ref name="SWCL" />

Along the riverside of the complex stood two-story anterooms with large window panes looking out on to the small parade grounds along the bank of the Solleu. The anteroom closest to the cliff's edge was known as the [[Great Hall (Naboo)/Legends|Great Hall]]; with marble floors and pillars soaring into the room's vaulted ceiling, the chamber was used by the Monarch for troop inspection during ceremonial parades. The other structure was the headquarters of the Security Force and home to a pilot training academy, equipped with a simulator program which conjured up the effects of an attack.<ref name="SWCL" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:ITW1_Theed_Hangar.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A cutaway of the Theed Hangar.]]
The Theed Hangar first appeared on-screen during the [[1999]] release of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. Several diagrams of the facility would later appear in the source books ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]'' and later again in [[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]. Within both these books, the hangar is depicted as resting to the left of the palace when viewing the city from the cliff side. However, the aerial view of Theed in the 2005 release of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] places the building on the right side of the palace as viewed from a similar angle. As the movies claim precedence, the hangars are fixed as being on the right side of the palace.

In the [[2000]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles]]'', the Jedi fight a battle in the hangar which contradicts [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. They engage [[Plasma battle droid]]s during their escape, but in the film, they are only confronted by standard battle droids.

[[File:BFN_rsf_headquarters.jpg|thumb|left|150px|The RNSF HQ as depicted in ''Star Wars: Battle for Naboo.'']]

While both above mentioned source books reference the hangar as the location of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]]' headquarters, the 2000 video game ''[[Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo]]'' depicts it as the headquarters as a different building made completely of stone with a broad staircase at its front. Whether or not this facility is meant to be a supplementary building, or simply game mechanics, is unknown at this time.
